role.description: `view`, `operate` or `admin`: each includes the ones before.

setup.description: Whether an admin may set the server up over the network.

subject.description: Whose access token it is, when it is one.

Applied.description:
What berth recorded on a host when it applied the configuration: its own
version and the plugins whose features the host has.

AppliedPlugin.description: A plugin as it was when a host's configuration was applied.

digest.description: SHA-256 of its files, so a change without a new version shows too.

sudo_password.description: The SSH user's sudo password, for a host that asks for one.

choices.description: A command whose lines are the values to offer.

Behind.description: How a host's configuration differs from what berth would apply now.

changes.description: berth first when its version changed, then the plugins.

features.description: What the server's plugins can install, in the order they are applied.

key.description:
The server's own SSH public key, which the operator of a host it sets
up takes unless the profile says otherwise.

template.description: The profile a new host starts from.

Change.description: Something that changed since a host was applied: berth itself or a plugin.

from.description: The version the host was applied with.

to.description:
The version there is now; empty for a plugin that is gone, the same
as `from` for one whose files changed.

lines.description: One line per thing checked, starting with ✓, ! or ✗.

FeatureInfo.description: Something a plugin installs, for the Features page of a host.

group.description: The group of the Features page it is listed in.

From.description: Who did something, as berthd saw it.

Generate.description: Something for the server to make up for a profile.

password.description:
For `password`: the password to hash. Without it one is made up and
kept beside the profile of `host`, under `user`.
A password that was made up, for whoever asked to write down.

value.description: The host name, the password's hash, or the key.

HostBehind.description: A host whose configuration is behind, and how.

applied.description:
The berth version its configuration was last applied with, when its
berthd says. An older berthd does not, nor does a host not applied
since.

oneOf.description: What changed since then, when the server would apply something else now.

next.description: Pass as `before` for older ones, when there are more.

seq.description: The order it was taken in; what `before` counts in.

InboxMessage.description: A stored message: the host's message with where it came from.

Instance.description: The machine berth created for a host.

created.description: When it was asked for, RFC 3339.

id.description: The provisioner's id of the machine; empty until `create` said it.

verbs.description: What can be done to it besides `destroy`: `start`, `stop`.

oneOf.description: How a roll-out went, host by host, once it has ended.

ListedInstance.description: A machine a provisioner has that berth created.

host.description: The host it was created for, as its labels say.

first_offset.description: Where what is still kept begins, when the start was dropped.

lines.description: The same as text, when read by lines.

offset.description: The offset this answer starts at.

PluginFeature.description: Something a plugin installs, switched on per host.

channels.description: Channel topics, without the plugin's id.

group.description: The group of the Features page it is listed in.

PluginInfo.description: A plugin that was found, with what it can install.

dir.description: Where it is on the machine that has it.

provisioners.description: What it can create machines with.

PluginList.description: The plugins a berth serve has, and where it keeps its own.

dir.description: The directory of its own plugins; a folder copied there is one too.

PluginOrigin.description: Where a plugin comes from, which says whether it can be removed.

PluginReport.description: What npm said of a change, a few lines; the first starts with ✓.

behind.description: After an update: the hosts whose configuration is now behind.

PluginService.description: A program a feature keeps running on the host to answer calls.

name.description: The service is `PLUGIN/NAME` on the host.

PluginSpec.description:
What npm installs, with the server's npm configuration and none of the
package's scripts.

spec.description:
A package of the server's npm registry, `[@SCOPE/]NAME[@VERSION]`, or
the https address of a .tgz.

PluginTask.description: A task a feature adds to a host's overview.

agent.description: The agent may run it with `box run`.

arguments.description: The names of the arguments it asks for.

extends.description: Tasks of berth it runs after, with no row of its own.

name.description: The task is `PLUGIN:NAME` on the host.

PluginUpdate.description: Whether a newer version of a plugin is there, as its registry says.

latest.description: The registry's latest version, when it is another one.

note.description:
Why there is nothing to ask, or what asking said: a plugin from a
.tgz or a folder has no registry to ask.

PluginUpdateSpec.description: What to update: one plugin by its id or npm name, or all of them.

PluginUpdates.description: The answer of `plugins.check`: each of the user's plugins.

Provision.description: What to create a host's machine with.

arguments.description: Values of its arguments; the others take their defaults.

ProvisionerInfo.description: Something a plugin creates machines with, for a saved host's profile.

missing_secrets.description: The required ones that have no value. Not looked at in a plugin's listing.

secrets.description: The berth secrets it is given.

setup.description:
`seed`: the machine boots with berth's cloud seed and sets itself up.
`apply`: berth applies the profile over SSH once the machine answers.

verbs.description:
What it can do besides `create`, `status` and `destroy`: `start`,
`stop`, `list`.

registries.description:
By name: `type` (nexus, npm, raw or docker), `url`, `username` and, for
a Nexus server, its `repositories`.

Rollout.description:
What a roll-out does: apply the hosts that are behind one after another,
stopping at the first that fails.

all.description: Also the hosts that are current.

force.description: Reboot although sessions run, which ends them.

hosts.description: These hosts, in this order; all saved hosts by name when empty.

reboot.description: Reboot a host that says it needs it, and wait for it to come back.

update.description: Run each host's `update` task after applying.

changes.description: What had changed, as it was before applying.

error.description: What went wrong, for a failed host.

warnings.description:
What did not go well without being a failure, such as an update step
that ended badly. One stops the roll-out after this host.

RolloutReport.description: The result of a roll-out, host by host in the order they were taken.

ok.description: Every host is done or current.

RolloutState.description: How one host of a roll-out went.

SecretNames.description:
The names of the secrets the server keeps. Their values never leave it
except to a host.

names.description: A registry's password or token is `registry/NAME`.

Seed.description: What a new machine is started with to become the host.

user_data.description: cloud-init user data, for the provider's field of that name.

lost.description: It ended with berthd or the host, not by itself.

task.description: The task it was started for, if any.

value.description: Empty when it is not set, and for a token.
Empty to go back to the default.

oneOf.description:
What the host's configuration was last applied from, when berth
recorded it. An older berthd does not say.

description: The operations of berth serve. Every operation of a host is one here too: on the portal with `"host": "NAME"` in the frame, over HTTP under /v1/hosts/NAME. Only the `secrets` task is refused; `hosts.secrets` sends the server's own. Each operation names the least role a caller over TCP needs: view, operate or admin.
